reason: 'Stipitate' was rejected as a part word (it is a quality). 'Stipitate gland' itself is fine as gland (PO_0005656), but glandular trichome (PO_0004509) is not always right: stalked glands on petioles and leaf teeth (Passiflora, Prunus, Euphorbiaceae) are not trichomes. The stalk is better kept as FLOPO:0991172 stipitate-glandular on the organ that bears the glands, and the singular is rare. Confidence low; keeping it as gland, the same as 'stalked gland' (R2795), would also be defensible.

Every stalked gland is a gland, so gland (PO_0005656, PO synonym 'gland') is a true parent. Glandular trichome (PO_0004509) would be wrong for the stalked glands on petioles and leaf teeth that are not hairs. The stalk is carried by FLOPO:0991172 stipitate-glandular on the organ that bears them.
'Discoid' was already rejected as a part word ('a shape quality of glands; the part is the gland'). So the bearer is the gland (PO_0005656), and the disc shape is a quality, not a kind of gland.
Plural of 'discoid gland'. The bearer is the gland (PO_0005656), and discoid is a shape quality, as in the rejected-word decision for 'discoid'.

The first check misread 'perfect'. On stamens it means fertile, not bisexual: the earlier rejected-word entry for 'perfect' sends 'stamens perfect' to fertile (PATO_0000955). The bearer is the stamen (PO_0009029), and PO has no fertile-stamen class.
Plural of 'perfect stamen'. The bearer is the stamen (PO_0009029), and 'perfect' is the fertility quality (PATO_0000955).

A stalked gland is a gland, so PO_0005656 is a correct parent. Glandular trichome (PO_0004509) is wrong for stalked glands that are not hairs (on petioles or leaf teeth). This matches the earlier rules that keep stalked glands apart from glandular hairs (R0889, R2005). The stalk goes to FLOPO:0991172 stipitate-glandular.
Plural of 'stalked gland'. Gland (PO_0005656) is a correct parent, and glandular trichome is not always right.
It is a cyme (PO_0030126). The umbel-like look is the quality FLOPO:0991031 umbelliform (synonym 'umbel-like', rule R0101), as decided for 'cymose-umbellate' (R1302). The bearer rule is right.
Same as 'umbel-like cyme': the bearer is the cyme (PO_0030126), and 'umbelliform' is the quality FLOPO:0991031.

The phrase includes the quality 'present', like the rejected 'stipe present'. A hair-point (the hyaline tip of a moss leaf) is part of the leaf apex, not the whole apex. It needs a presence statement or a hair-pointed apex value, not a bearer rule.

Umbel and anthela rays are primary inflorescence branches (PO_0006321 has the exact synonym 'primary inflorescence branch'). Bare 'rays' also means ray flowers (PO_0025331) and wood rays (PO_0025411), so it needs an inflorescence context.

In seed-plant floras 'sex organs' means androecium plus gynoecium, which is a union with no single class. Gametangium (PO_0025124) fits only bryophytes and ferns, and a part constraint cannot separate the two meanings.
Same as 'sex organ': stamens plus pistil in flowering plants, gametangia only in bryophytes. No single class covers it.
In French floras 'organes sexuels' means androecium and gynoecium together. Gametangium is wrong, and no single class covers both.

A secondary bract is a bract (PO_0009055), so the parent is correct. Order words like 'secondary' are not kept as parts (the rejected 'secondary' and 'secondary lobe'), and the organ is named here. PO has no class for bracts on branches of a given order.
Plural of 'secondary bract'. Bract (PO_0009055) is a correct parent, and the order is not a part.
French form of 'secondary bracts'. Bract (PO_0009055) is a correct parent.

PO itself lists 'colpi' as a NARROW synonym of canal (PO_0025132), whose definition covers a groove on the surface of a structure. A pollen colpus is such a groove, so the first check's 'wrong' is too strict. Limit it to pollen so fruit furrows are not caught.
'Colpus' is a NARROW PO synonym of canal (PO_0025132), a surface groove. That is right for a pollen aperture furrow, so limit it to pollen.
'Colpé' (having colpi) is an adjective, not a part. Counts like '3-colpé' belong to the count-of-parts pattern on the colpus.

It can mean a conifer cone scale (megasporophyll PO_0009027, which already has its own 'cone scale' rule), a fruiting glume or scale in Cyperaceae, or the bracteoles of Atriplex. Fertile lemma is wrong, and the word is ambiguous.

Under the corolla, the galea is the hooded upper corolla lip (Lamiaceae, Orobanchaceae), so corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017) is a correct parent, as for 'upper lip' (R2628). The hood shape is the quality galeate/cucullate (R0224). The orchid sense (a hood of sepals and petals) must not match.

This matches 'male spike' and 'staminate spike', which go to staminate inflorescence (R2416/R2417). A pistillate spike is a pistillate inflorescence, so the sex is kept by the class and not left to a separate quality.
Disk scales are separate scale-like parts of the disc, and what they are varies by family. The whole floral disc (FLOPO_0986025) is the wrong bearer, and no class for a part of the disc exists.
Labellum lobe (FLOPO_0986028) is right only for the orchid lip. 'Lip' can also be the corolla lip (the rejected 'lip limb'), so the rule applies only under the labellum.

'Stipe' already maps to stalk (PO_0025066) through the accepted rule C264, and 'stipe' is a PO synonym of stalk. The organ it holds up is a container or context matter, not a reason to drop the rule. Low confidence: in French floras the word may often be 'stipité' (stalked), which is a quality, so the rule needs a check against the source text.
Plural of 'stipe', which is a PO synonym of stalk (PO_0025066) and already has rule C264. The organ is a matter of context.

The stipe of a pollinarium is a stalk (PO_0025066) by the PO definition (an elongated part that holds up another part). There is no pollinarium class to use as a container, so stalk is the best existing class.
This is ambiguous. It can be an epidermal scale (a trichome, as in ferns) or a scale leaf (cataphyll, PO_0006003, in seed plants). No single class or part constraint resolves it.
